Memory's updated. Here's the full picture for the meeting.

## The reframe

This isn't a Sprint 3 retro — it's Sprint 3 Planning Day. Jira confirms the real Sprint 3 runs **11–24 Aug** (both squads) and starts *today*; Confluence's own Meeting Cadences page defines Tuesday as "Sprint Planning (First day of Sprint)." Neither squad's Sprint 3 page has a goal or committed stories yet. So "Meeting: Components" is very likely the working session that shapes what gets committed today — which is exactly why the story-writing *approach* needs to be settled first.

(Side note: the local `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` planning doc is stale — it mislabels this window as "Sprint 4" and claims "Sprint 3" already happened 27 Jul–7 Aug with PDP/PLP/Cart/Search feature work. That work never shipped — the 268-commit git history and 51 PRs are almost entirely CI/CD, tagging, and governance work, which lines up with what real Jira Sprint 2 actually contained: environment spikes and config, not features. I've corrected this in memory; flagging it here since you may want to get that file refreshed separately. Happy to do it if you want.)

## The methodology is already drafted — this is likely the actual agenda

Two Confluence pages were edited as recently as yesterday/today, with zero comments — meaning nobody's weighed in yet:

- **[04.7 Component Inventory](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/400195591)** — a live tracker mapped 1:1 to the Figma design-system file, with per-component Status and a "Sprint Planning" column already tagging most ready components **"Sprint 3 for User Story Writing 2026-08-11 – 2026-08-24."**
- **[04.71 Writing User Stories for Components](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/400195600)** — the actual proposal. It defines two levels:
  - **Level 1 — Component epics** (the build story): PWA-Kit-only components (Button, Textfield, Dropdown, Cart Item) get **one** story. Components that also need Contentful authoring (Banner, Editorial Cards, Footer, Navigation) get **two** — one in the Contentful epic, one in PWA Kit — because "a Contentful component always needs a PWA Kit story too; a PWA-Kit-only component does not need a Contentful story."
  - **Level 2 — Page epics** (the experience story — PDP/PLP/Checkout): shopper-perspective, how components compose on the page, explicitly must **not** repeat Level 1 build detail.

This is walking distance from what a "Tim" precedent already established informally (shared config → component → page integration) — 04.71 mostly formalizes it and adds the PWA-Kit-vs-Contentful story-count rule.

## It's already live in Jira, as of this morning

**Isabel "Izzy" Chaloner** (the other Delivery Lead, who Tash covers for) created six **"EXAMPLE:"** tickets between 11:56am–12:15pm today, under the real components epic **SFCC-2 "PWA Kit Components"**:
- [SFCC-691](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-691)/[692](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-692)/[694](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-694) — Title and Link Component × PWA Kit / Contentful / PDP
- [SFCC-698](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-698)/[699](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-699)/[700](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-700) — Editorial Cards Module × Contentful / PWA Kit / PLP

Both source components are deliberately picked from the inventory's "Not Confirmed" rows — these are teaching examples, not real backlog. **One thing worth raising directly**: the "— PDP" and "— PLP" tickets (which read as Level 2 page-integration stories) are apparently *also* parented under SFCC-2 rather than under the PDP/PLP page epics (SFCC-5/SFCC-6). Worth confirming whether that's deliberate or just simplified for the example — it's a concrete edge case the meeting should nail down either way.

## Evidence the pattern already works — bring these as proof points

Across the four live page epics, the atomic-story pattern is already dominant, not aspirational: **Cart** (SFCC-11, 20 stories — e.g. separate tickets for Product Info Display, Quantity Stepper, Total Section, Bag Overlay, Disclaimer), **PLP** (SFCC-6, 17), **PDP** (SFCC-5, 18), **Search** (SFCC-7, 19). The clearest textbook example: [SFCC-195](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-195) covers only the PDP "Details & Care" slide-out tab — siblings SFCC-102, 267, 266, 101 cover the other tabs as separate stories. And the shared-enabler chain is real: [SFCC-104](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-104) (BM config) → [SFCC-108](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-108) (filter UI component) → [SFCC-199](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-199) (PLP integration, already Ready For Review).

**Good counter-examples to name as "before" cases**: [SFCC-90](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-90) "Homepage Layout & Content Modules UI" bundles 6 distinct content modules into one 5-point story with no split. SFCC-52/SFCC-55 (Global Header/Footer) are partially decomposed but still bundle multiple components each.

## Real blocker to raise: design sign-off gates what's actually writable now

The Definition of Ready states "stories with UI components are not Ready without approved designs." Cart, Search, and PLP are **100% pending** on the page-level design tracker (unchanged since 13 Jul). But the component-level tracker (04.7) shows many atomic PWA-Kit components — Button, Textfield, Dropdown, Footer pieces, Navigation, PDP Hero, Product Card Base, Recently Viewed, etc. — are design-confirmed and already tagged for this sprint. **Practical implication for the meeting**: Sprint 3's realistic scope is writing Level 1 (PWA-Kit-only) component stories now, while Level 2 page epics and Contentful-linked stories for Cart/Search/PLP stay blocked until their designs land. Worth proposing that split explicitly rather than letting it be assumed.

There's also an unresolved dependency worth flagging if it comes up: `.docs/temp/openItems.md` records that SFCC-vs-Contentful content ownership on *composed* pages (which editorial blocks appear on PDP/PLP) is still unconfirmed — which makes it genuinely ambiguous, for a handful of components, which epic(s) a Level 1 story even belongs in.

## Documentation gaps worth naming out loud

- 04.71 has **zero comments** — it hasn't been socialized with the team yet, so today may be its first real airing.
- No cross-link either direction between 04.71 and **["Creating User Stories with Claude"](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/274137093)** (the BA's guide to Jira story mechanics — AC format, labels, FE/BE split) — worth asking whether these should reference each other.
- Development Standards / Component Override Strategy (code-level docs) already imply one-folder-per-component granularity with a mandatory Storybook story — i.e., the codebase's own organizing unit already matches what 04.71 proposes for stories. Worth pointing out as validation: the code structure and the new story structure agree.

## Where you specifically fit in

As the frontend lead spanning both squads, you're well placed to own consistency of whatever pattern gets ratified today across Squad A and Squad B — especially since CODEOWNERS already treats shared components (product-tile, display-price, swatch-group, etc.) as individually owned/reviewed units, which is the same "isolate by component" instinct the meeting is trying to formalize at the story level. Also worth a heads-up: CODEOWNERS assigns PDP/PLP ownership to Squad B and Cart/Checkout to Squad A — if the old sprintScope.md's "Squad A does PDP/PLP" framing comes up in the room, it's worth reconciling against that.

## Quick people reference

- **Tash = Natasha Lay**, Accenture Delivery Lead (Sydney — explains the office booking), covering for Izzy Chaloner. Process/governance decision-maker, not Scrum Master or BA.
- **Izzy Chaloner** — the other Delivery Lead, actively seeding the example tickets today.
- **Hazel Cacalda** — Scrum Master, both squads.
- **Jasmijn Tsang** — Lead BA, authored the earlier informal precursor split (SFCC-648/650).

Customer appointment history surfaces within My Account, read directly from the Booxi API by the PWA's Managed Runtime Node layer via `/mobify/proxy/booxi/...`. This is a **PWA-direct path** — it does **not** transit SFCC or MuleSoft.
6	
7	The requirement covers appointment history display only (CRM-165–167); storefront scope and timeline are still TBC. This document describes the integration shape so the section can be slotted in later without rework; the precise contract is finalised once Booxi confirms its API (see §11).
8	
9	In scope of this document:
10	
11	- Appointment history list rendered inside My Account, read PWA → MRT → Booxi (CRM-165)
12	- The MRT proxy leg that holds the Booxi credential and identifies the customer to Booxi
13	- Embedding, loading, error and retry behaviour observed by the customer in the browser

16

18	- Any SFCC or MuleSoft involvement — there is none on this path.
19	
20	## 2. Vendor relationship
21	
22	- **Vendor:** Booxi — appointment scheduling platform; system of record for Zimmermann boutique appointment data (CRM-166).
23	- **PWA's relationship:** Booxi is consumed read-only. The API contract is owned by Booxi / the Zimmermann CRM team; the PWA team is not a co-developer of the API.
24	
25	## 3. Browser-side architecture
26	
27	The flow below is the recommended design. It is not yet a fixed contract — the customer-identification mechanism is pending confirmation with Booxi (see §11), and the specifics below would change if another scheme is agreed.
28	
29	```
30	Browser (My Account → Appointments section)
31	        │  Customer's SLAS access token (JWT) is present after SFCC login
32	        ▼
33	PWA fetches /mobify/proxy/booxi/<endpoint>
34	   Authorization: Bearer <SLAS access token>
35	        │
36	        ▼
37	MRT Node layer:
38	   1. Validates the SLAS JWT signature against SFCC's published JWKS
39	   2. Drops the inbound Authorization header and sets the Booxi credential
40	      header instead (Booxi authenticates via its own `Booxi-PartnerKey`
41	      header, not a bearer `Authorization` header)
42	   3. Resolves the customer's Booxi identity (see §4) and scopes the request to it
43	   4. Forwards to https://<booxi-host>/<endpoint>
44	        │
45	        ▼
46	Booxi API:
47	   • Authorises the request via the Booxi API credential
48	   • Returns the customer's appointment history
49	        │
50	        ▼
51	Booxi response → MRT → Browser (typed JSON, only the fields the section needs)
52	```
53	
54	- The browser never carries the Booxi credential. The Booxi API credential is held as an MRT environment variable and is appended only on the MRT → Booxi leg.
55	- The appointments section is read-only and authenticated — it renders only for a logged-in customer on the My Account route.
56	- The section is built as a self-contained module so it can be enabled when Booxi is ready without restructuring the surrounding My Account page (CRM-167).
57	
58	## 4. Authentication and credentials
59	
60	| Credential | Where used | Sensitivity |
61	|---|---|---|
62	| Booxi Partner API key (sent in the `Booxi-PartnerKey` header) | MRT environment variable; injected by MRT before forwarding | Secret — Booxi mandates this key is used server-side only and never reaches the browser |
63	| Customer SLAS access token (JWT) | Forwarded from the browser to MRT; used by MRT to authenticate the customer | Sensitive — proves user identity |
64	| SFCC JWKS | Used by MRT to verify the SLAS JWT signature | Public |
65	
66	- **No Booxi credential in the browser bundle.** The Booxi credential is held server-side as an MRT environment variable, appended on the MRT → Booxi leg only.
67	- **Customer identification (open — see §11).** The PWA must prove *which* customer's appointments to return without letting the browser request an arbitrary customer's data. The recommended approach is that MRT validates the customer's SLAS JWT and resolves the corresponding Booxi customer reference server-side (from a Booxi customer ID held on the SFCC/Omneo profile, or via a Booxi lookup), then scopes the request to that reference. MRT must never accept a raw Booxi customer ID, email, or appointment ID from the browser as the identity input.
68	- One Booxi API credential per environment. Rotation cadence and named owner are tracked in §11.
69	
70	## 5. Data exchanged
71	
72	| Direction | Data | Notes |
73	|---|---|---|
74	| Browser → MRT | Customer JWT (SLAS access token); endpoint path | The browser never sees the Booxi credential and never passes a customer identifier as input. |
75	| MRT → Booxi | Booxi API credential; customer-scoped identifier resolved server-side | The credential authorises the channel; the resolved identity scopes the data. |
76	| Booxi → MRT → Browser | Typed JSON — appointment history (date/time, boutique, appointment type, status) | MRT projects only the fields the My Account section renders. |
77	
78	The customer sees only their own appointment data, which they already own. No payment data is involved on this path.
79	
80	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
81	
82	- The appointment history read fires only when the My Account appointments section is in view — it does not preload on the dashboard or any other route.
83	- TanStack Query caches the appointment history response on the client; stale data is acceptable for history display.
84	- The My Account appointments module is route-level code-split so it adds nothing to other route bundles, and so it can ship dark until Booxi is enabled (CRM-167).
85	- `<link rel="preconnect">` to the Booxi host is emitted from the My Account routes once the customer is authenticated and the section is enabled.
86	
87	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
88	
89	- Appointments are boutique-bound; the history list reflects whichever boutiques the customer has booked with, independent of the storefront locale.
90	- A single Booxi tenant is assumed across all eight storefronts; per-region boutique availability is configured in Booxi, not in the PWA.
91	- Locale affects only the display formatting of dates and labels in the storefront, not the Booxi request.
92	
93	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
94	
95	Each external system must fail independently — a Booxi outage must not break the My Account page.
96	
97	| Failure | Behaviour |
98	|---|---|
99	| MRT cannot verify the SLAS JWT (expired, invalid) | Return 401 to the browser without calling Booxi. The storefront triggers a silent SLAS refresh and retries; if refresh fails, force re-login. |
100	| Booxi 5xx or timeout on the history read | Suppress the appointments section (or show a compact "appointments temporarily unavailable" state with a retry CTA) rather than throwing. The rest of My Account renders normally. Never block the page on Booxi. |
101	| Customer has no appointment history | Render an explicit empty state, not an error. |
102	| Customer is unauthenticated on the route | Standard My Account authentication redirect. No Booxi request is issued. |
103	| Booxi rotates or revokes the API credential | Rotation is handled in the MRT environment configuration by the integration team. No browser-side change required. |
104	
105	## 9. Security and privacy
106	
107	- The Booxi API credential is held as an MRT environment variable and never appears in browser JavaScript, request URLs, or logs. MRT redacts the Authorization header in its access logs.
108	- The customer's SLAS JWT is forwarded to MRT only over TLS 1.2+ and is not forwarded to Booxi as a raw identity token — MRT resolves the customer-scoped Booxi reference server-side so the browser cannot request another customer's data.
109	- No appointment identifier or customer reference is accepted from the browser as an input to the request.
110	- The browser calls the same-origin MRT proxy path (`/mobify/proxy/booxi/...`) — no CSP `connect-src` entry for Booxi's host is needed; MRT makes the server-side call to Booxi outside the browser's CSP boundary.
111	- On a right-to-erasure request (REG-060–067), removal of appointment data in Booxi is handled by the CRM/integration team through Booxi's own erasure process; the storefront has no separate erasure flow for Booxi data.
112	
113	## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation
114	
115	1. **Storefront scope (CRM-165 – CRM-167).** Confirm whether the My Account appointments surface is read-only history (current assumption) or whether in-storefront booking / rescheduling / cancellation is also in scope. Until confirmed, the section is built read-only and structured to slot in without redesign.
116	2. **Booxi API specification.** Booxi to publish the API contract for appointment history — endpoint(s), request and response schemas, the appointment status values and their customer-facing copy, error codes, and pagination. The PWA-side types are generated from this contract.
117	3. **Customer-identification mechanism (PWA-direct path).** Confirm how the storefront proves customer identity to Booxi without allowing the browser to retrieve an arbitrary customer's appointments. Confirm whether a Booxi customer ID is stored on the SFCC/Omneo profile (and how it is populated), or whether MRT must look the customer up in Booxi at request time. The mechanism must prevent impersonation.
118	4. **Per-environment Booxi credentials.** Booxi to supply, per environment: Booxi API host, API credential, and the credential rotation cadence and named owner. Note the API host is region-specific (e.g. a North America vs EU base URL), so confirm which regional host serves Zimmermann.

|---|---|---|
| Browser → MRT | Customer JWT (SLAS access token); endpoint path | The browser never sees the Booxi credential and never passes a customer identifier as input. |
| MRT → Booxi | Booxi API credential; customer-scoped identifier resolved server-side | The credential authorises the channel; the resolved identity scopes the data. |
| Booxi → MRT → Browser | Typed JSON — appointment history (date/time, boutique, appointment type, status) | MRT projects only the fields the My Account section renders. |

The customer sees only their own appointment data, which they already own. No payment data is involved on this path.

## 6. Performance and loading strategy

- The appointment history read fires only when the My Account appointments section is in view — it does not preload on the dashboard or any other route.
- TanStack Query caches the appointment history response on the client; stale data is acceptable for history display.
- The My Account appointments module is route-level code-split so it adds nothing to other route bundles, and so it can ship dark until Booxi is enabled (CRM-167).
- `<link rel="preconnect">` to the Booxi host is emitted from the My Account routes once the customer is authenticated and the section is enabled.

## 7. Multi-region behaviour

- Appointments are boutique-bound; the history list reflects whichever boutiques the customer has booked with, independent of the storefront locale.
- A single Booxi tenant is assumed across all eight storefronts; per-region boutique availability is configured in Booxi, not in the PWA.
- Locale affects only the display formatting of dates and labels in the storefront, not the Booxi request.

## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation

Each external system must fail independently — a Booxi outage must not break the My Account page.

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| MRT cannot verify the SLAS JWT (expired, invalid) | Return 401 to the browser without calling Booxi. The storefront triggers a silent SLAS refresh and retries; if refresh fails, force re-login. |
| Booxi 5xx or timeout on the history read | Suppress the appointments section (or show a compact "appointments temporarily unavailable" state with a retry CTA) rather than throwing. The rest of My Account renders normally. Never block the page on Booxi. |
| Customer has no appointment history | Render an explicit empty state, not an error. |
| Customer is unauthenticated on the route | Standard My Account authentication redirect. No Booxi request is issued. |
| Booxi rotates or revokes the API credential | Rotation is handled in the MRT environment configuration by the integration team. No browser-side change required. |

## 9. Security and privacy

- The Booxi API credential is held as an MRT environment variable and never appears in browser JavaScript, request URLs, or logs. MRT redacts the Authorization header in its access logs.
- The customer's SLAS JWT is forwarded to MRT only over TLS 1.2+ and is not forwarded to Booxi as a raw identity token — MRT resolves the customer-scoped Booxi reference server-side so the browser cannot request another customer's data.
- No appointment identifier or customer reference is accepted from the browser as an input to the request.
- The browser calls the same-origin MRT proxy path (`/mobify/proxy/booxi/...`) — no CSP `connect-src` entry for Booxi's host is needed; MRT makes the server-side call to Booxi outside the browser's CSP boundary.
- On a right-to-erasure request (REG-060–067), removal of appointment data in Booxi is handled by the CRM/integration team through Booxi's own erasure process; the storefront has no separate erasure flow for Booxi data.

## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation

1. **Storefront scope (CRM-165 – CRM-167).** Confirm whether the My Account appointments surface is read-only history (current assumption) or whether in-storefront booking / rescheduling / cancellation is also in scope. Until confirmed, the section is built read-only and structured to slot in without redesign.
2. **Booxi API specification.** Booxi to publish the API contract for appointment history — endpoint(s), request and response schemas, the appointment status values and their customer-facing copy, error codes, and pagination. The PWA-side types are generated from this contract.
3. **Customer-identification mechanism (PWA-direct path).** Confirm how the storefront proves customer identity to Booxi without allowing the browser to retrieve an arbitrary customer's appointments. Confirm whether a Booxi customer ID is stored on the SFCC/Omneo profile (and how it is populated), or whether MRT must look the customer up in Booxi at request time. The mechanism must prevent impersonation.
4. **Per-environment Booxi credentials.** Booxi to supply, per environment: Booxi API host, API credential, and the credential rotation cadence and named owner. Note the API host is region-specific (e.g. a North America vs EU base URL), so confirm which regional host serves Zimmermann.

I'm researching a specific technical question for the Zimmermann Salesforce PWA Kit project (Confluence space key SFCC, site zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net). A team member named Kiera asked a colleague (nickname "Angelo") whether there's a planned "out of the box" (i.e. pre-built third-party library, not custom-built) solution for a calendar/date-picker component shown in a specific Figma screen (file "Zimmermann_Designs", node-id 3193-47937). The screenshot shows: a "Find in Boutique" panel/flyout, with "SIGNED IN AS ANGELA LEE", a "CHOOSE A DATE" section with a full month calendar grid (June 2026, showing all days of the month, one date highlighted/selected), an "AVAILABLE TIMES" section with clickable time slot buttons (9:00AM through 4:00PM), and a "CONTINUE" button at the bottom. The Figma layers panel shows this sits under a "Find in Boutique" grouping alongside other layers like "FIND IN BOUTIQUE modal open" variants.

Important context/discrepancy I've already found in the local repo's requirement docs (.docs/prd/*.md and .docs/integration/*.md):
- "Find in Boutique" is documented as a stock/inventory-check flyout only — it shows per-boutique product availability for a selected product+size via a MuleSoft call, using Google Maps + geolocation (PDP §8, CAI-037–042, PRD-028–039, OM-031). Nothing in its documented spec involves a calendar, date picker, or appointment time slots.
- Booxi (a third-party appointment-scheduling vendor) is the actual system that handles appointments, but the current confirmed PWA scope for Booxi (CRM-165–167) is READ-ONLY appointment history display in My Account only — appointment creation/booking is explicitly documented as "not in current PWA scope... handled in Booxi's own surfaces," with storefront booking scope/timeline still "TBC" (to be confirmed).
- So a date+time-slot BOOKING calendar doesn't cleanly match either documented feature as currently scoped — it could mean the docs are stale/outdated, or this represents a scope expansion (in-storefront Booxi booking now confirmed?) that hasn't been written back into the local integration doc yet, or it's a different/new feature not yet documented locally at all (e.g. a private styling appointment, personal shopping, or "reserve to view in store" feature).
- Also: no calendar or date-picker npm package is installed in package.json at all currently, and there's no existing calendar-related code anywhere in the codebase — so if a decision on an "out of the box" library was made, it hasn't been implemented in code yet, meaning any record of the decision would only exist in Confluence or Jira.
- One more related data point: the PRD also separately documents a gift-card delivery date picker (giftcards.md, GC-005/GC-006) — "calendar with month navigation; restricted to within 3 months from today" — a DIFFERENT feature that also needs a calendar UI. If the team already evaluated/chose a calendar library for that, it might be the same one intended for reuse here — worth checking too.

1. **Does Booxi's in-storefront booking scope look more confirmed/expanded in Confluence than the local docs suggest?** Search for "Booxi" pages beyond what a prior pass found (integration register, TSDs). 2. **Is there a technical decision, spike, or evaluation doc about a calendar/date-picker component specifically?** Search broadly: "calendar", "date picker", "datepicker", "react-day-picker", "react-datepicker", "react-calendar", "flatpickr", "react-dates", "MUI date", "Chakra date", "out of the box". Also check whether Development Standards (261750785) or Component Override Strategy (261881857) or the newer "04.7 Component Inventory" (400195591)/"04.71 Writing User Stories for Components" (400195600) pages mention a calendar/date component or name a specific library.

3. **Is there a page specifically about "Find in Boutique"?** Search for it directly — check if Confluence's version of this feature's spec differs from (or is more current than) the local .docs/prd/pdp.md and .docs/integration/03-mulesoft.md descriptions I summarized above. Does Confluence show it including a booking/appointment step, or purely a stock-check flyout as the local docs say?

4. **Gift card delivery date picker (GC-005/006)** — search for any Confluence page (requirements sheet mirror, TSD, or spike) discussing the gift card scheduled-delivery calendar UI and whether a specific library/approach was chosen for it.

5. **Any Figma-adjacent tech notes** — check if there's a "Web Design (UX)" or Design Tracker page, or any dev-handoff/tech-feasibility notes, that references this specific Figma frame/flow (a boutique appointment booking calendar with "Choose a Date" + "Available Times" + Continue) and names an implementation approach.

Report back with page titles, IDs, last-modified info, and concrete content summaries/quotes for each question — I need to know definitively whether an "out of the box" calendar solution was actually decided, and if so which one, or whether this is genuinely still an open/undecided question (in which case say so clearly rather than guessing). I'm researching a specific technical question for the Zimmermann Salesforce PWA Kit project (Confluence space key SFCC, site zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net). A team member named Kiera asked a colleague (nickname "Angelo") whether there's a planned "out of the box" (i.e. pre-built third-party library, not custom-built) solution for a calendar/date-picker component shown in a specific Figma screen (file "Zimmermann_Designs", node-id 3193-47937). The screenshot shows: a "Find in Boutique" panel/flyout, with "SIGNED IN AS ANGELA LEE", a "CHOOSE A DATE" section with a full month calendar grid (June 2026, showing all days of the month, one date highlighted/selected), an "AVAILABLE TIMES" section with clickable time slot buttons (9:00AM through 4:00PM), and a "CONTINUE" button at the bottom. The Figma layers panel shows this sits under a "Find in Boutique" grouping alongside other layers like "FIND IN BOUTIQUE modal open" variants.

Important context/discrepancy I've already found in the local repo's requirement docs (.docs/prd/*.md and .docs/integration/*.md):
- "Find in Boutique" is documented as a stock/inventory-check flyout only — it shows per-boutique product availability for a selected product+size via a MuleSoft call, using Google Maps + geolocation (PDP §8, CAI-037–042, PRD-028–039, OM-031). Nothing in its documented spec involves a calendar, date picker, or appointment time slots.
- Booxi (a third-party appointment-scheduling vendor) is the actual system that handles appointments, but the current confirmed PWA scope for Booxi (CRM-165–167) is READ-ONLY appointment history display in My Account only — appointment creation/booking is explicitly documented as "not in current PWA scope... handled in Booxi's own surfaces," with storefront booking scope/timeline still "TBC" (to be confirmed).
- So a date+time-slot BOOKING calendar doesn't cleanly match either documented feature as currently scoped — it could mean the docs are stale/outdated, or this represents a scope expansion (in-storefront Booxi booking now confirmed?) that hasn't been written back into the local integration doc yet, or it's a different/new feature not yet documented locally at all (e.g. a private styling appointment, personal shopping, or "reserve to view in store" feature).
- Also: no calendar or date-picker npm package is installed in package.json at all currently, and there's no existing calendar-related code anywhere in the codebase — so if a decision on an "out of the box" library was made, it hasn't been implemented in code yet, meaning any record of the decision would only exist in Confluence or Jira.
- One more related data point: the PRD also separately documents a gift-card delivery date picker (giftcards.md, GC-005/GC-006) — "calendar with month navigation; restricted to within 3 months from today" — a DIFFERENT feature that also needs a calendar UI. If the team already evaluated/chose a calendar library for that, it might be the same one intended for reuse here — worth checking too.

Please research Confluence (space SFCC) and report back on:

1. **Does Booxi's in-storefront booking scope look more confirmed/expanded in Confluence than the local docs suggest?** Search for "Booxi" pages beyond what a prior pass found (integration register, TSDs). Check if there's a newer/updated Booxi TSD, spike, or requirements page that confirms in-storefront appointment booking (not just history) is now in scope. Also check the CRM-165/166/167 requirement rows directly if you can find the source requirements sheet or its Confluence mirror.

2. **Is there a technical decision, spike, or evaluation doc about a calendar/date-picker component specifically?** Search broadly: "calendar", "date picker", "datepicker", "react-day-picker", "react-datepicker", "react-calendar", "flatpickr", "react-dates", "MUI date", "Chakra date", "out of the box". Also check whether Development Standards (261750785) or Component Override Strategy (261881857) or the newer "04.7 Component Inventory" (400195591)/"04.71 Writing User Stories for Components" (400195600) pages mention a calendar/date component or name a specific library.

3. **Is there a page specifically about "Find in Boutique"?** Search for it directly — check if Confluence's version of this feature's spec differs from (or is more current than) the local .docs/prd/pdp.md and .docs/integration/03-mulesoft.md descriptions I summarized above. Does Confluence show it including a booking/appointment step, or purely a stock-check flyout as the local docs say?

4. **Gift card delivery date picker (GC-005/006)** — search for any Confluence page (requirements sheet mirror, TSD, or spike) discussing the gift card scheduled-delivery calendar UI and whether a specific library/approach was chosen for it.

5. **Any Figma-adjacent tech notes** — check if there's a "Web Design (UX)" or Design Tracker page, or any dev-handoff/tech-feasibility notes, that references this specific Figma frame/flow (a boutique appointment booking calendar with "Choose a Date" + "Available Times" + Continue) and names an implementation approach.

Report back with page titles, IDs, last-modified info, and concrete content summaries/quotes for each question — I need to know definitively whether an "out of the box" calendar solution was actually decided, and if so which one, or whether this is genuinely still an open/undecided question (in which case say so clearly rather than guessing). This is read-only research — do not create, edit, or comment on any Confluence content. Keep the report focused and organized under the 5 numbered questions; it will be read by another Claude session synthesizing an answer, not an end user directly.

content.content:
- Per-size availability shown (ADD TO BAG / OUT OF STOCK / low-stock "LOW" indicator)
- **ADD TO BAG** shown when quantity is above buffer threshold
- **OUT OF STOCK** shown when quantity is at or below buffer threshold (back-in-stock capture presented)
- Low-stock indicator at size level — no quantity number shown — displays "LOW" label
- **Max 3 units per SKU** (same size + colour) enforced at add-to-cart (CAI-017, confirmed)
- **No soft reservation** at add-to-cart (CAI-032, confirmed)

---

## 7. Primary CTAs & Supporting Links (PRD-018 – PRD-022, confirmed)

- **Add to Bag** — primary CTA when in stock
- **Find in Boutique** — opens as a **slide-out** (not a modal) alongside Add to Bag (PRD-018)
- **Wishlist icon** — displayed alongside the primary CTA; size must be selected before wishlist save (PRD-019, PRD-020)
- Supporting links: **Unavailable** (opens slide-out notify me form), **Find My Size**, **Size Guide** (PRD-021)
- **Need Assistance** section: links to email, live chat (with availability hours caveat), and Contact Us (PRD-022). The "Contact Us" link is an external redirect to the Zendesk-hosted contact form — there is no embedded Zendesk integration in the storefront.

---

## 8. Find in Boutique (CAI-037 – CAI-042, PRD-028 – PRD-039)

The "Find in Boutique" CTA is shown on all eligible products. The feature opens as a **flyout/slide-out panel** (not a modal). All Find in Boutique requirements are now **confirmed** but carry a **Phase 2** design caveat (design not yet available — "Phase 2").

### Panel contents
- "Find in Boutique" CTA only displays for products where in-store stock checking is supported (PRD-028, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- At top of panel: product thumbnail, product name, selected colour, and price (PRD-029, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- **Size selector** pre-populated from the PDP selection; customer can change size within the panel (PRD-030, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- A **real-time inventory call** to NewStore via MuleSoft is made once a size is selected; the call refreshes when the customer selects a different size (CAI-038)
- **No auto-refresh** while the panel is open; boutique stock cached with configurable TTL (CAI-042)
- **Location search field** to filter boutique results (PRD-031, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- **"Use My Location"** option triggers browser geolocation with explicit permission; handles failure case gracefully with inline message (PRD-032, PRD-033, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- **Maps integration** via Google Maps (via MRT API connection) for boutique directions (PRD-034, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- Per-boutique results show: name, address, distance (if geolocation permitted), stock status (**In Stock / Low Stock – Contact Boutique to Confirm Availability / Out of Stock**), opening hours, contact details, current live open status (e.g. "OPEN – CLOSES AT 6:00PM"), map pin, and a view more button (PRD-035, confirmed). Opening hours and live open status are sourced from the **Google Business API** (with a manual override available in Business Manager) — distinct from the Google Maps integration used for the map pin and directions (TPI: Google Business API; Google Maps).
- **Get Directions** link per boutique result, opening the location in a maps application (PRD-036, confirmed)
- Configurable limit on number of boutique results displayed (PRD-039, confirmed)
- Display a clear message when no boutiques carry the selected size (CAI-041)
- **No buffer stock** applied to boutique inventory (CAI-040)
- Fully responsive across desktop, tablet, and mobile (PRD-037, confirmed)
- Enter key triggers search in the location field (PRD-038, confirmed)

content.content:
# PRD – Gift Cards & Credit Notes

*Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheet "Gift Cards & Credit Notes" (GC). Last updated: 2026-06-07.*

*All GC requirements are **Confirmed** (signed off 2026-05-12 by Emma, Rebecca; sign-off date 2026-06-01). GC-049 max-cards limit remains open (see §12).*

---

## 1. Scope

Gift cards and credit notes are available on **domestic storefronts only** (AU, UK, EU, US). Not available on Global-e international storefronts (HK, ME, US Int, EU Int) at launch — international gift card support is on the future roadmap (GC-050).

Two types:
- **Physical gift card** — delivered by post
- **Digital gift card** — delivered by email on a scheduled date

Both types are processed by **GiveX**. Both types are tax-exempt across all storefronts (GC-020).

---

## 2. Gift Card PDP (GC-001 – GC-008)

- Customer selects an amount from **fixed denominations: $100, $200, $250, $300, $500** via a searchable dropdown — applies to both physical (GC-001, GC-002) and digital (GC-003, GC-004) gift cards
- Customer enters: sender name, recipient name, recipient email address, delivery date, and optional personal message (GC-001, GC-003)
- **Delivery date picker**: calendar with month navigation; restricted to within 3 months from today; future dates beyond 3 months are greyed out (GC-005, GC-006)
- Recipient email is validated for format before Add to Bag is enabled (GC-007)
- Sender and recipient may be the same person (GC-008)

---

## 3. Mini-Cart (GC-009 – GC-010)

- Gift card displayed in mini-cart: gift card image, price, quantity only (GC-009)
- Actions: **Move to Wishlist (physical cards only)**, Remove (GC-010)

---

## 4. Cart Page

### Digital gift card (GC-011 – GC-015)

content.content:
- **CRM-162–164:** Private marketing URL grants access to exclusive VIC products without requiring login or customer group at browse time; VIC Exclusive tag shown on PLP and PDP; purchase restricted to eligible customer group regardless of access method. Enhancement logged for personalised content for loyalty customers across the site. See also Section 4.

### Communication Preferences (CRM-174–177, all Confirmed)

- Rendered as an **Omneo iFrame** embedded in My Account (CRM-174 — enhancement logged to move into SFCC). **No — there's no "out of the box" calendar solution decided anywhere.** Checked the codebase (no date-picker package installed, no calendar code exists), JIRA (zero tickets or comments mention react-day-picker, react-datepicker, react-calendar, flatpickr, or any other library — clean full-text search across the whole project), and Confluence (same — no evaluation/spike doc, and the component-inventory design-system catalogue doesn't even list a Calendar/DatePicker component). If this was discussed, it never got written down anywhere the team keeps records.

## But there's a bigger issue worth raising with Kiera first

That screen doesn't actually match **"Find in Boutique"** as currently scoped, and this isn't just a documentation-wording thing — it's confirmed at the API level. Find in Boutique's real MuleSoft contract is just `{ProductId, CountryCode} → [{StoreId, qty}]` — a stock check, no date or time field exists in it anywhere. Every PRD section and every related Jira story (SFCC-297, 308, 458) describes it purely as a location-search-and-stock flyout.

What the screen actually looks like is **Booxi appointment booking** — but that's scoped as **read-only appointment history only** (CRM-165–167, Confirmed). Booking itself isn't planned as a self-service calendar at all right now: the only documented booking mechanism today is a **live-chat handoff** (Confluence INT-027, Inside Chat — "boutique appointment booking" via the chat widget, status Under Review). The whole Loyalty & Appointments design area is still Phase 2 / Pending / not signed off, with no Figma link even populated in the tracker yet.

My best guess (not confirmed anywhere): the Figma file likely just groups this under "Find in Boutique" because both are boutique-related slide-out panels, not because it's the same feature. Worth a quick "hey, is this actually the Booxi appointment flow, and has self-service booking been confirmed to replace the chat handoff?" before answering the calendar-library question at all — otherwise you might end up scoping a library for a flow that isn't actually planned yet.

## One adjacent data point

The only other calendar UI confirmed anywhere in the project is the gift-card delivery date picker (GC-005/006, [SFCC-386](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-386)) — much simpler (date-only, no time slots). It's undecided too — no library named, and its own design isn't signed off either. So if a "standard" calendar solution ever does get picked, that's the natural place it'd first apply, and this boutique screen would presumably reuse it.

Saved the full trail to memory since this is a real gap that'll come up again. Want me to draft an actual reply message to send Kiera, or hold off until you confirm the scope question with her?

# Special Components

:::note
This guide assumes that you’re familiar with how routing works in a PWA Kit storefront. To learn more, see our guide to [Routing](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/routing.md).
:::

The PWA Kit React SDK includes the following special components: `AppConfig`, `App`, `Error`, and `Document`.

The default implementation of each special component can be overridden by your own custom version so that you can configure and customize the behavior of your storefront across multiple pages.

Let’s look at each special component separately:

## AppConfig

The `AppConfig` component is positioned near the top of the component hierarchy in your React app. From this position, it allows you to insert code to configure and support app-wide features, such as [state management](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/managing-global-state.md) or component theming. In the Retail React App, the `ChakraProvider` component is inserted into `AppConfig` to make theme values (for colors, spacing, and so on) available to all the [Chakra UI](https://chakra-ui.com/) components.

The `AppConfig` component also lets you extend the set of arguments that get passed to all components that are enhanced by `routeComponent` via the `getProps` function. To add these arguments, define a function called `extraGetPropsArgs` as a property of the `AppConfig` component.

The Retail React App uses the `extraGetPropsArgs` function to give all components that are enhanced by `routeComponent` access to an object for interacting with the Salesforce Commerce API:

```javascript
AppConfig.restore = (locals = {}) => {
  locals.api = new CommerceAPI(apiConfig)
}

AppConfig.freeze = () => undefined

AppConfig.extraGetPropsArgs = (locals = {}) => {
  return {
    api: locals.api
  }
}
```

The version of the `AppConfig` component from the PWA Kit React SDK doesn’t do much—unless you override it. To override the SDK version of `AppConfig`, define a file in `app/components/_app-config/index.jsx`. A newly generated PWA Kit project already includes this file to get you started.

## App

The `App` component is a child of the `AppConfig` component. Its main purpose is to include any components for layout and UI that persist throughout your React app, such as the header, footer, and sidebar.

The `App` component is also enhanced by the `routeComponent` function. If you define a `getProps` function as a property of the `App` component, it gets called when *any* component from the `routes` array is rendered. Use it for any logic that you’d like to run on every page.

Like `AppConfig`, a default version of the `App` component exists in the PWA Kit React SDK, and you’re encouraged to override it. To override the SDK version of `App`, define a file in `app/components/_app/index.jsx`. A newly generated PWA Kit project already includes this file to get you started.

Some of the features that are implemented in `App` for a newly generated project include: analytics tracking, offline detection, and the `SkipNavLink` component for accessibility.

## Error

The `Error` component is rendered in place of the `App` component under any of the following conditions:

- The user makes a request for a path that isn’t found in the `routes` array.
- A component from the `routes` array throws an error in its `getProps` function.
- A component from the `routes` array throws an error during rendering.

When the `Error` component is returned, an HTTP 404 status is also included in the response header.

Like the other special components, the PWA Kit React SDK includes a default version of the `Error` component, and you’re encouraged to override it. To override the SDK version of `Error`, define a file in `app/components/_error/index.jsx`. A newly generated PWA Kit project already includes this file to get you started.

By overriding the `Error` component, you can do things like customize the error page for your brand, add redirects, and track the error as an analytics event.

## Document

The `Document` component defines the HTML that surrounds your application, such as the `<html>`, `<head>`, and `<body>` tags.

Like the other special components, the PWA Kit React SDK includes a default version of the `Document` component that can be overridden. But, in this case, we *don’t* recommend that you override it. But if you need fine-grained control over your application, you can override `Document` by defining a file in `app/components/_document/index.jsx`. A newly generated PWA Kit project does *not* include this file.

:::tip
Rather than override the `Document` component, we recommend using the [React Helmet](https://www.npmjs.com/package/react-helmet) library to modify the HTML tags in `Document`, such as `<head>`.
:::

The most practical options for a Chakra-based team would be `react-day-picker` (the most widely adopted, accessible, and pairs naturally with Chakra styling), `chakra-dayzed-datepicker` (a Chakra-specific wrapper), or Adobe's `react-aria` primitives for more robust accessibility. ## Research Report: "Book a Fitting" / Charmaine Lew / Kiera Rikard-Bell in Jira (project SFCC)

### 1. "Book a Fitting" / "fitting" — direct search results

**No ticket in the SFCC project documents a "Book a Fitting" flow.** Every search angle came up empty or returned false positives:

- `text ~ "fitting"` → 14 hits, all false positives from Jira's stemming (matches "Fit"/"Fitted"/"fits" anywhere in text): PDP slide-out stories, SEO tickets, `Ask Charmaine...` subtasks, spikes, etc. None describe a booking flow.

This looked significant at first, but reading the full comment shows it's a pure false positive from JQL's term-matching (not true phrase-matching): the comment contains "**price books**" (G3–G7 gap list) and "**Fitted** Blouse" (product example name) — i.e., stemmed "book" + stemmed "fit" appearing independently, nothing about appointment booking. **This is not a real hit.**
- `text ~ "fitting appointment"` → 0 hits.
- `summary ~ "fitting"` (narrower) → only SFCC-207 (Charmaine accordion-tabs subtask, matched on "does not seem to **fit** in current design") and SFCC-102 "PDP – Slide Out - **Size & Fit**" — neither is booking-related.
- `cf[10231] ~ "fitting"` (searching the separate **Acceptance Criteria** custom field, `customfield_10231`, which the default `text ~` search does **not** index) → same false positives (SFCC-266, SFCC-195, SFCC-102, SFCC-90), all stemming noise, nothing new.
- `cf[10231] ~ "Booxi" OR "Booksy" OR "calendar" OR "appointment"` → **zero hits, project-wide.** No Acceptance Criteria anywhere in SFCC mentions any of these terms.
- Synonym sweep (`consultation`, `styling session`, `schedule`, `book now`, `reserve a fitting`) → 33 hits, all false positives (Global-e jobs, category scheduling, opening-hours feeds, etc.) — nothing related.
- Recent-ticket sweep (all PDP/Store Locator children created in the last 14 days) → 33 tickets, all granular Store Detail/Locator UI stories (hours table, map, contact block, etc.) or standard PDP stories (wishlist, Find in Boutique, Shipping & Returns) — no booking/calendar/fitting title.

**Conclusion: "Book a Fitting" is not an existing Jira ticket, story, or AC anywhere in the SFCC project — under any wording I could construct.**

### 2. Charmaine Lew

Confirmed as a **real, resolvable Jira user**: `jira_get_user_profile` succeeded on `charmaine.lew@accenture.com` → display name "Charmaine Lew". She does **not** appear as an assignee or reporter anywhere — she's referenced only as a third-party design contact inside subtask titles/comments authored by the dev team:

- **SFCC-207** — "Ask Charmaine on how accordion tabs work in desktop design (can be up to 7 times, does not seem to fit in current design)" (Done; subtask of **SFCC-195** "PDP – Slide Out - Details & Care", parent epic SFCC-5 PDP). Comment by Dani Rivett: *"Charmaine has added a gradient to show more items horizontally"*.
- **SFCC-211** — "Ask Charmaine to design error messaging on PDP - max purchase quantity" (Done; subtask of SFCC-196 "PDP UI – Maximum Purchase Quantity").
- **SFCC-208** — "Discuss the to-be Chat functionality with Rebecca - then with Charmaine on how that should function, where and when chat should appear / position on each page" (To Do; subtask of SFCC-267 "PDP – Slide Out – Shipping & Returns and Assistance").
- Also turned up (via broader text match, not opened in full) in several other PDP/PLP ticket comment threads: SFCC-203, SFCC-199, SFCC-194, SFCC-150, SFCC-92, SFCC-28.

**Assessment:** Charmaine Lew is an established, actively-engaged UX/UI designer specifically on PDP-related design decisions (accordion behaviour, error messaging, chat placement) around the same period as the Figma comment (subtasks created 2026-07-21, close to the "~12 days ago" comment date). Nothing in these tickets mentions fitting, Booxi, or a calendar — but she is clearly a legitimate, active design authority the frontend lead would expect to see commenting on a PDP-adjacent Figma screen.

### 3. Kiera Rikard-Bell

Also confirmed as a **real, resolvable Jira user**: `kiera.rikard-bell@accenture.com` → display name "Kiera Rikard-Bell". Same pattern as Charmaine — no assignee/reporter role, only referenced by first name in comments:

- **SFCC-255** — "Discuss Size Selector - Recommendation in design review Friday" (In Progress; subtask of **SFCC-101** "PDP – Slide out - Measmerize Widget & Find My Size CTA"). Comment by Jasmijn Tsang: *"had a chat with Kiera and User:712020:c99d37b3-9c93-4347-951d-5ffb32ff1341 yesterday - the idea is now to have 'Recommended: 2' displayed on PDP next to the size selector, replacing 'Find My Size'..."*
- **SFCC-236** — "Product Card Shared Component" (Ready For Review; under SFCC-2 PWA Kit Components). Comment: *"The product card behaviour on the 'see full recently viewed' page was not specified in the design - I asked Kiera - she recommended to keep the behaviour similar to product card on PLP."*
- **SFCC-648** — "pdp/size-selector" (To Do; under SFCC-2) also matched the `Kiera` text search, but its description/comments show no visible "Kiera" mention — likely a search artifact, not a genuine reference. Treat as inconclusive.

**Assessment:** This re-confirms (rather than overturns) the prior pass's finding — SFCC-255 and SFCC-236 are about **PDP sizing UX** (size-selector recommendation wording, product-card behaviour), not Find in Boutique or fitting appointments. "Find in Boutique" is **not a single epic** — it's a cross-cutting feature split across three different epics, confirmed by re-pulling all three stories plus their parents and issue links:

- **SFCC-297** "PDP UI — Find in Boutique Button and Slide-In Panel" (In Refinement; parent **SFCC-5** PDP epic). Description: *"This story covers the PWA Kit frontend component for Find in Boutique on the PDP. **No child/linked/sibling ticket about booking a fitting exists anywhere under any of these three parent epics.** The feature as ticketed today is stock-check-only, exactly as previously understood.

### 5. Booxi / Booksy / Personal Styling — and a genuine naming inconsistency

"Personal Styling" and "Find in Boutique" are **confirmed as two separate, unrelated concepts** in the current backlog — but a real documentation inconsistency surfaced around the appointment vendor's name:

- **SFCC-16** "Customer Account & CRM" (Epic). Its own description says, in three separate places: *"Appointments section within My Account (**Booksy** integration — storefront scope and timelines TBC)"*; *"**Booksy** — appointment data source for My Account appointments section (scope TBC)"*; *"**Booksy** platform configuration — Zimmermann scope"* (Out of Scope); and *"Appointments section storefront scope and delivery timelines are **TBC** pending further scoping with Zimmermann"* (Assumptions).
- **SFCC-72** "**Booxi** Appointment History Integration" (To Do; child of SFCC-16). Description: *"Placeholder story - appointment history sourced from Booxi API."* Read-only history only — matches your prior understanding.
- **SFCC-626** "My Account – Services Page Layout" (To Do; child of SFCC-16). Description: *"...Personal Styling tile with 'Book an Appointment' link (**routes to Booxi** — dependency: SFCC-72), Gift Cards tile..., and Care Guides tile. The Appointments section is built as a **placeholder** to accommodate the Booxi integration (SFCC-72) **without requiring structural redesign when it is ready**."* Acceptance Criteria field is null (unrefined).
- **SFCC-525** "Store Detail – Boutique Services Section" (To Do; child of **SFCC-9** Store Locator, not SFCC-16). Description: *"...Each service is presented as a tile containing a service heading, a short description, and a CTA link (e.g. 'Book an Appointment' for Personal Styling, 'Make a Reservation' for Click and Reserve)."* Same CTA-link pattern, surfaced on the Store Detail page instead of My Account. Acceptance Criteria field is also null.

**So: the epic (SFCC-16) says "Booksy," while both of its own child stories (SFCC-72, SFCC-626) say "Booxi."** These are two different real-world commercial products (Booxi = retail/luxury appointment-booking and clienteling platform; Booksy = salon/beauty booking app) — this is either a straightforward, uncorrected typo in the epic description, or a genuine unresolved ambiguity about which vendor is actually contracted. Either way, it has never been reconciled in Jira, and it's directly relevant to your Figma sticky-note finding (Charmaine Lew's *"Dev team to confirm Out of the box calendar"*) — that comment reads as exactly this same open question (is the calendar Booxi/Booksy's own out-of-the-box hosted widget, vs. something Zimmermann must build?), still unresolved anywhere in Jira.

Both stub stories (SFCC-626, SFCC-525) have zero Acceptance Criteria written, and the epic (SFCC-16) explicitly flags the whole Appointments section as **"TBC"**. This "Book an Appointment" concept also lives under **My Account** and the **Store Detail page** — never under PDP or "Find in Boutique."

### Bottom line

"Book a Fitting" as a PDP → Find in Boutique sub-flow with an in-storefront calendar/time-slot/Continue booking UI **does not exist as a ticket, story, AC, or even a passing text mention anywhere in Jira** — this was checked via full-text search, the separate Acceptance Criteria custom field, synonym variations, and a 14-day recency sweep. The closest conceptual relative already ticketed is "Personal Styling → Book an Appointment" (SFCC-16/72/626/525), but that is scoped to My Account and Store Detail pages as an external link/placeholder to Booxi (per SFCC-72/626) or "Booksy" (per SFCC-16 itself) — not PDP/Find-in-Boutique, not an embedded calendar, and explicitly still "TBC." The frontend lead's confirmation that this Figma screen is specifically "Find in Boutique → Book a Fitting" describes a linkage that is genuinely new/undocumented in Jira as of today (2026-08-11) — the Figma comment thread (Charmaine Lew, ~2026-07-30, tagging Kiera Rikard-Bell and the frontend lead, 1 reply not visible to this research) currently appears to be the only record of this decision anywhere, and it lives in Figma, not Jira.</result>

---
name: project-calendar-component-gap
description: "No out-of-the-box calendar/date-picker exists anywhere — not in code/Jira/Confluence, not in Chakra 2.7.0, not in the base retail-react-app template; the Figma screen showing a date+time booking calendar doesn't match any currently-scoped feature"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  modified: 2026-08-11T05:46:56.947Z
  originSessionId: 0f890293-1d3d-4726-bb0d-646b77d58f77
---

**Triggered by:** Kiera asking the user ("Angelo" — Marcel Angelo Navarro) whether an "out of
the box" calendar solution was decided for a Figma screen (file "Zimmermann_Designs", node-id
3193-47937) showing "CHOOSE A DATE" (month calendar grid) + "AVAILABLE TIMES" (time-slot
buttons) + "CONTINUE", filed under a "Find in Boutique" Figma page/layer grouping.

**Clean negative result, checked across all four surfaces:** no calendar/date-picker npm
package is installed (`package.json`), no calendar code exists anywhere in `overrides/`, no
Jira ticket names a library (react-day-picker/react-datepicker/react-calendar/flatpickr/
react-dates all zero hits, full-text across summary+description+comments), and no Confluence
page discusses one either. **04.7 Component Inventory** (400195591, the design-system
catalogue) has no Calendar/DatePicker entry at all. Nobody has written this decision down
anywhere the team keeps records — if Kiera/Angelo discussed it, it never made it past verbal/
Slack.

**The screen doesn't match "Find in Boutique" as currently scoped — confirmed at the API level,
not just PRD prose.** Find in Boutique's actual MuleSoft contract (Confluence "Find In Store —
Boutique Stock Availability" TSD, id 292487173) is literally `{ProductId, CountryCode} →
[{StoreId, qty}]` — no date/time field exists in the integration at all. Every PRD source
(pdp.md §8, cart.md §7, orderManagement.md, Jira SFCC-297/308/458/307) agrees: it's a
location-search + geolocation + per-boutique stock/hours/maps flyout, nothing else.

**What the screen most likely actually is: Booxi appointment booking — but that's scoped
read-only history only, not self-service booking.** CRM-165/166/167 (Confirmed) cover only
displaying appointment *history* in My Account (Jira: SFCC-72 "Booxi Appointment History
Integration," description literally "Placeholder story"; SFCC-626 "My Account – Services Page
Layout" describes a "Book an Appointment" link that just *routes to Booxi* externally).
**The only currently-documented booking mechanism at all is a human handoff**: Confluence
"Store Details" register (258441217), **INT-027 Inside Chat** — "Live chat widget available on
Store Detail page for click-and-collect queries and boutique appointment booking" (Status:
Under Review) — not a self-service calendar. The whole Loyalty & Appointments design area is
Phase 2, tracker status PENDING/PENDING, no Figma link populated in the tracker at all.

**Most likely explanation (inference, not confirmed by any source):** the Figma file probably
groups this screen under "Find in Boutique" by *UI pattern* (both are boutique-related side-out
panels) rather than by requirement/epic — i.e. it's a design-file IA artifact, not evidence that
booking is now in scope. Worth confirming directly with whoever owns the Figma file / Booxi
scope rather than assuming either way.

**Confirmed 2026-08-11 it's not a Zimmermann-specific oversight either — the underlying stack
has no calendar solution at any layer.** Checked `node_modules` directly: Chakra UI 2.7.0 is
installed (transitively via `@salesforce/retail-react-app`, not a direct top-level dependency)
and has **no Calendar/DatePicker package among its ~70 `@chakra-ui/*` sub-packages** — Chakra
has never shipped one natively, by design (confirmed by direct inspection, not assumption).
`date-fns` is present (transitive, formatting only). The base `@salesforce/retail-react-app`
template itself — Salesforce's own reference storefront — has zero calendar-related code or
dependency anywhere in its source or `package.json` either, per user-provided reference docs
`~/Dev/pwa-kit-overview.md` and `~/Dev/pwa-kit-special-components.md` (the latter confirms
`ChakraProvider` is wired into the `AppConfig` special component — overridden here at
`overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx` — as the sole source of theming/component
system; neither doc mentions a calendar special component). **So whatever gets used here will
be a genuinely new decision** — either a new npm dependency (needs integration-team approval
per AGENTS.md Hard Rule #7 — common Chakra-ecosystem options: `react-day-picker`,
`chakra-dayzed-datepicker`, react-aria's `Calendar`/`DateField`) or a custom Chakra-primitives
build — not a "did we miss an existing option" gap.

**Related, smaller data point:** the only other confirmed calendar requirement in the entire
project is the gift-card delivery date picker (GC-005/GC-006, Jira SFCC-386, date-only, no time
slots, "restrict to 3 months, grey out beyond"). It **also** has zero library/technical
decision on record and its own Design Tracker row is Pending/Pending — so even the one calendar
UI the project does confirm hasn't had a "how do we build this" conversation captured anywhere
either. If a library ever does get chosen, GC-005/006 is the natural first place to apply it,
and reuse it for any future boutique-booking calendar too.

**How to apply:** don't tell a colleague a library was "already decided" — it wasn't, anywhere.
If in-storefront Booxi booking scope gets confirmed later (superseding INT-027's chat-handoff
plan), this is the first place to record which calendar library gets chosen, since nothing
currently exists to point to.

Related: [[reference_confluence_sfcc]], [[project_real_sprint_cadence]].

**How to apply:** don't tell a colleague a library was "already decided" — it wasn't, anywhere.
If in-storefront Booxi booking scope gets confirmed later (superseding INT-027's chat-handoff
plan), this is the first place to record which calendar library gets chosen, since nothing
currently exists to point to.

**Update 2026-08-11 — the screen is actually "Find in Boutique → Book a Fitting" (per the
frontend lead directly), and this is exhaustively confirmed undocumented anywhere.** A
second, deeper research pass (local grep + full Confluence/Jira sweep including Jira's
separate Acceptance-Criteria custom field and synonym variants) found **zero mentions of
"fitting"/"Book a Fitting" anywhere** — not one page, ticket, or AC field, under any phrasing.
"Find in Boutique" itself is re-confirmed, now even more exhaustively, as stock-check-only
across all three tickets that implement it (SFCC-297 PDP panel, SFCC-308 real-time stock,
SFCC-458 buffer-stock exclusion) — none has a calendar, time slot, booking step, or
signed-in-customer display in its Acceptance Criteria.

**Closest existing relative in the backlog: "Personal Styling → Book an Appointment"**
(epic SFCC-16, stories SFCC-72/626, plus SFCC-525 on the Store Detail page) — but this lives
under **My Account** and **Store Detail**, not PDP/Find in Boutique, and every instance
describes a CTA that **routes externally** to Booxi/Booksy rather than an embedded
calendar+time-slot+Continue UI. SFCC-16 explicitly flags the whole Appointments section as
"TBC"; SFCC-626 and SFCC-525 both have **zero Acceptance Criteria written**.

**The Booxi/Booksy naming split may be more than a typo — treat as genuinely unresolved, not
settled.** "Booksy" (CRM-165/166, Third Party Integrations, epic SFCC-16 itself) and "Booxi"
(Third Party Overview, TSD, SFCC-72/626, and Confluence's "04.6 Consent Management — Business
Overview" — the one place describing it as "**boutique appointment booking | Required |
Functional booking tool**," not just history) are used inconsistently across both Confluence
and Jira, with no page/ticket reconciling them. An earlier pass recorded "TT confirmed Booxi,
Booksy is the typo" — that likely still holds (Booxi is a retail/luxury clienteling platform,
a natural fit for a fashion brand; Booksy is a mass-market salon/beauty booking app, a poor
fit) — but it has evidently never been corrected consistently, so don't assume it's fully
settled without asking. This doesn't change the earlier Booxi Booking Widget research (still
the most likely candidate "out of the box" answer if in-storefront booking is real), but the
naming ambiguity itself is worth surfacing.

**People, now confirmed:**
- **Charmaine Lew** (`charmaine.lew@accenture.com`) — Product Designer, Accenture, Melbourne,
  works across both squads ("Squad Oversight"). Actively engaged on PDP-adjacent design calls
  in Jira around the same time as her Figma sticky note (subtasks dated 2026-07-21, note dated
  ~2026-07-30): accordion behaviour (SFCC-207), error messaging (SFCC-211), chat placement
  (SFCC-208). A credible, legitimate source — her "Dev team to confirm Out of the box calendar"
  note reflects a genuine open question, not confusion on her part.
- **Kiera Rikard-Bell** (`kiera.rikard-bell@accenture.com`) — real Accenture person, confirmed
  resolvable in both Confluence and Jira user directories, but **zero formal footprint** in
  either (no roster entry, no assignee/reporter role, no authored page). Referenced only
  informally as someone the team consults for UX judgment calls: SFCC-255 (size-selector
  recommendation wording) and SFCC-236 (product-card behaviour on Recently Viewed) — both
  unrelated to fitting/Booxi/calendars. Her actual role/seniority can't be pinned down from
  these systems — genuinely unknown, not worth guessing.

**Highest-value next step, more true now than before:** the Figma comment thread on this exact
screen (Charmaine's note, ~2026-07-30, tagging Kiera + the user, **1 reply already posted**)
is now confirmed to likely be the *only* record of this decision anywhere — Jira and
Confluence have both been exhaustively searched and come back empty. Reading that reply
directly is worth more than further repo/Jira/Confluence digging at this point. A parallel
MS Copilot sweep of Teams/Outlook was also kicked off 2026-08-11 to check for anything outside
these systems.

Related: [[reference_confluence_sfcc]], [[project_real_sprint_cadence]].

---
name: project-calendar-component-gap
description: "No out-of-the-box calendar/date-picker exists anywhere — not in code/Jira/Confluence, not in Chakra 2.7.0, not in the base retail-react-app template; the Figma screen showing a date+time booking calendar doesn't match any currently-scoped feature"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  modified: 2026-08-11T06:09:01.341Z
  originSessionId: 0f890293-1d3d-4726-bb0d-646b77d58f77
---

**Triggered by:** Kiera asking the user ("Angelo" — Marcel Angelo Navarro) whether an "out of
the box" calendar solution was decided for a Figma screen (file "Zimmermann_Designs", node-id
3193-47937) showing "CHOOSE A DATE" (month calendar grid) + "AVAILABLE TIMES" (time-slot
buttons) + "CONTINUE", filed under a "Find in Boutique" Figma page/layer grouping.

**Clean negative result, checked across all four surfaces:** no calendar/date-picker npm
package is installed (`package.json`), no calendar code exists anywhere in `overrides/`, no
Jira ticket names a library (react-day-picker/react-datepicker/react-calendar/flatpickr/
react-dates all zero hits, full-text across summary+description+comments), and no Confluence
page discusses one either. **04.7 Component Inventory** (400195591, the design-system
catalogue) has no Calendar/DatePicker entry at all. Nobody has written this decision down
anywhere the team keeps records — if Kiera/Angelo discussed it, it never made it past verbal/
Slack.

**The screen doesn't match "Find in Boutique" as currently scoped — confirmed at the API level,
not just PRD prose.** Find in Boutique's actual MuleSoft contract (Confluence "Find In Store —
Boutique Stock Availability" TSD, id 292487173) is literally `{ProductId, CountryCode} →
[{StoreId, qty}]` — no date/time field exists in the integration at all. Every PRD source
(pdp.md §8, cart.md §7, orderManagement.md, Jira SFCC-297/308/458/307) agrees: it's a
location-search + geolocation + per-boutique stock/hours/maps flyout, nothing else.

**What the screen most likely actually is: Booxi appointment booking — but that's scoped
read-only history only, not self-service booking.** CRM-165/166/167 (Confirmed) cover only
displaying appointment *history* in My Account (Jira: SFCC-72 "Booxi Appointment History
Integration," description literally "Placeholder story"; SFCC-626 "My Account – Services Page
Layout" describes a "Book an Appointment" link that just *routes to Booxi* externally).
**The only currently-documented booking mechanism at all is a human handoff**: Confluence
"Store Details" register (258441217), **INT-027 Inside Chat** — "Live chat widget available on
Store Detail page for click-and-collect queries and boutique appointment booking" (Status:
Under Review) — not a self-service calendar. The whole Loyalty & Appointments design area is
Phase 2, tracker status PENDING/PENDING, no Figma link populated in the tracker at all.

**Most likely explanation (inference, not confirmed by any source):** the Figma file probably
groups this screen under "Find in Boutique" by *UI pattern* (both are boutique-related side-out
panels) rather than by requirement/epic — i.e. it's a design-file IA artifact, not evidence that
booking is now in scope. Worth confirming directly with whoever owns the Figma file / Booxi
scope rather than assuming either way.

**Confirmed 2026-08-11 it's not a Zimmermann-specific oversight either — the underlying stack
has no calendar solution at any layer.** Checked `node_modules` directly: Chakra UI 2.7.0 is
installed (transitively via `@salesforce/retail-react-app`, not a direct top-level dependency)
and has **no Calendar/DatePicker package among its ~70 `@chakra-ui/*` sub-packages** — Chakra
has never shipped one natively, by design (confirmed by direct inspection, not assumption).
`date-fns` is present (transitive, formatting only). The base `@salesforce/retail-react-app`
template itself — Salesforce's own reference storefront — has zero calendar-related code or
dependency anywhere in its source or `package.json` either, per user-provided reference docs
`~/Dev/pwa-kit-overview.md` and `~/Dev/pwa-kit-special-components.md` (the latter confirms
`ChakraProvider` is wired into the `AppConfig` special component — overridden here at
`overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx` — as the sole source of theming/component
system; neither doc mentions a calendar special component). **So whatever gets used here will
be a genuinely new decision** — either a new npm dependency (needs integration-team approval
per AGENTS.md Hard Rule #7 — common Chakra-ecosystem options: `react-day-picker`,
`chakra-dayzed-datepicker`, react-aria's `Calendar`/`DateField`) or a custom Chakra-primitives
build — not a "did we miss an existing option" gap.

**Related, smaller data point:** the only other confirmed calendar requirement in the entire
project is the gift-card delivery date picker (GC-005/GC-006, Jira SFCC-386, date-only, no time
slots, "restrict to 3 months, grey out beyond"). It **also** has zero library/technical
decision on record and its own Design Tracker row is Pending/Pending — so even the one calendar
UI the project does confirm hasn't had a "how do we build this" conversation captured anywhere
either. If a library ever does get chosen, GC-005/006 is the natural first place to apply it,
and reuse it for any future boutique-booking calendar too.

**How to apply:** don't tell a colleague a library was "already decided" — it wasn't, anywhere.
If in-storefront Booxi booking scope gets confirmed later (superseding INT-027's chat-handoff
plan), this is the first place to record which calendar library gets chosen, since nothing
currently exists to point to.

**Update 2026-08-11 — the screen is actually "Find in Boutique → Book a Fitting" (per the
frontend lead directly), and this is exhaustively confirmed undocumented anywhere.** A
second, deeper research pass (local grep + full Confluence/Jira sweep including Jira's
separate Acceptance-Criteria custom field and synonym variants) found **zero mentions of
"fitting"/"Book a Fitting" anywhere** — not one page, ticket, or AC field, under any phrasing.
"Find in Boutique" itself is re-confirmed, now even more exhaustively, as stock-check-only
across all three tickets that implement it (SFCC-297 PDP panel, SFCC-308 real-time stock,
SFCC-458 buffer-stock exclusion) — none has a calendar, time slot, booking step, or
signed-in-customer display in its Acceptance Criteria.

**Closest existing relative in the backlog: "Personal Styling → Book an Appointment"**
(epic SFCC-16, stories SFCC-72/626, plus SFCC-525 on the Store Detail page) — but this lives
under **My Account** and **Store Detail**, not PDP/Find in Boutique, and every instance
describes a CTA that **routes externally** to Booxi/Booksy rather than an embedded
calendar+time-slot+Continue UI. SFCC-16 explicitly flags the whole Appointments section as
"TBC"; SFCC-626 and SFCC-525 both have **zero Acceptance Criteria written**.

**The Booxi/Booksy naming split may be more than a typo — treat as genuinely unresolved, not
settled.** "Booksy" (CRM-165/166, Third Party Integrations, epic SFCC-16 itself) and "Booxi"
(Third Party Overview, TSD, SFCC-72/626, and Confluence's "04.6 Consent Management — Business
Overview" — the one place describing it as "**boutique appointment booking | Required |
Functional booking tool**," not just history) are used inconsistently across both Confluence
and Jira, with no page/ticket reconciling them. An earlier pass recorded "TT confirmed Booxi,
Booksy is the typo" — that likely still holds (Booxi is a retail/luxury clienteling platform,
a natural fit for a fashion brand; Booksy is a mass-market salon/beauty booking app, a poor
fit) — but it has evidently never been corrected consistently, so don't assume it's fully
settled without asking. This doesn't change the earlier Booxi Booking Widget research (still
the most likely candidate "out of the box" answer if in-storefront booking is real), but the
naming ambiguity itself is worth surfacing.

**People, now confirmed:**
- **Charmaine Lew** (`charmaine.lew@accenture.com`) — Product Designer, Accenture, Melbourne,
  works across both squads ("Squad Oversight"). Actively engaged on PDP-adjacent design calls
  in Jira around the same time as her Figma sticky note (subtasks dated 2026-07-21, note dated
  ~2026-07-30): accordion behaviour (SFCC-207), error messaging (SFCC-211), chat placement
  (SFCC-208). A credible, legitimate source — her "Dev team to confirm Out of the box calendar"
  note reflects a genuine open question, not confusion on her part.
- **Kiera Rikard-Bell** (`kiera.rikard-bell@accenture.com`) — real Accenture person, confirmed
  resolvable in both Confluence and Jira user directories, but **zero formal footprint** in
  either (no roster entry, no assignee/reporter role, no authored page). Referenced only
  informally as someone the team consults for UX judgment calls: SFCC-255 (size-selector
  recommendation wording) and SFCC-236 (product-card behaviour on Recently Viewed) — both
  unrelated to fitting/Booxi/calendars. Her actual role/seniority can't be pinned down from
  these systems — genuinely unknown, not worth guessing.

**Highest-value next step, more true now than before:** the Figma comment thread on this exact
screen (Charmaine's note, ~2026-07-30, tagging Kiera + the user, **1 reply already posted**)
is now confirmed to likely be the *only* record of this decision anywhere — Jira and
Confluence have both been exhaustively searched and come back empty. Reading that reply
directly is worth more than further repo/Jira/Confluence digging at this point. A parallel
MS Copilot sweep of Teams/Outlook was also kicked off 2026-08-11 to check for anything outside
these systems.

Related: [[reference_confluence_sfcc]], [[project_real_sprint_cadence]].
